title: Offline regrade inherits ambient provider credentials
claim: The fresh verifier process inherits the caller environment, including ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, while env.json declares credential_free=true. The explicit projection denylist does not sanitize inherited variables.

evidence.detail: Only material.verifier_env is checked for credential-shaped names.
Command inherits the environment; only three named variables are removed; no env_clear.
The regression checks env.json projected keys, not the actual child environment.

title: Regrade has no production dispatch into Harbor or Pier
claim: Preparation pins tools/uv as verifier_executable, but regrade starts it with zero arguments and only private OPI_EVAL_REGRADE variables. No production consumer launches the pinned native grader or restores artifacts into a verifier environment. The environment-variable grading implementation exists only in the test stand-in.

evidence.detail: The verifier is cache/tools/uv, validated as uv 0.9.7.
Four private regrade variables are emitted; lines 757-767 start the executable without argv.
The shell stand-in alone interprets OPI_EVAL_REGRADE and compares synthetic marker bytes to manufacture a fresh job.

title: Result admission accepts substituted terminal product, build and model
claim: A native job with the expected outer integration name can seal a score even when its terminal record says product=oracle, executable hash differs from the selected build and its result model is unrelated. Those fields are parsed or copied but not checked against the selection.

evidence.detail: model_info.name is imported without equality to the frozen selected model.
Terminal observation is parsed, then delivered artifact digests are checked; selected terminal product/build are not compared.
Product and executable hash are accepted as arbitrary strings.

title: Native provider failures enter the Agent score denominator
claim: Harbor/Pier integrations map every nonzero Agent exit to NonZeroAgentExitCodeError and do not decode native JSON terminal errors. Native settlement treats that exception as a graded Agent failure and never invokes the existing native-client terminal parsers. Captured authentication errors therefore enter valid Agent scores; an error stream at exit zero has the same disconnected parser boundary.

evidence.detail: All nonzero exits raise NonZeroAgentExitCodeError; the Pier sibling does the same at line 348.
The final classifier consumes upstream exception tags, not the actual client error stream.
A synthetic AgentRecord is built from exit/timeout; stdout/stderr and usage default empty.

title: Declared execution deadlines are not enforced by native dispatch
claim: Resolved execution time_limit_seconds, agent_timeout_seconds and verifier_timeout_seconds are displayed/frozen but do not reach the native process dispatch; adapters retain profile limits. A one-second declared limit allows each synthetic job to sleep two seconds and still complete and score.

evidence.detail: The three execution deadlines are parsed into ResolvedExecution.
Preview narrows and displays the configured deadline.
Native trial dispatch does not consume the ResolvedExecution deadline fields.

title: Documented run --plan plus --native-material panics
claim: The CLI permits --plan with --native-material while --plan excludes --config. The native material branch unconditionally expects config, so the documented combination panics with exit 101 before file validation. Both README examples also omit the still-required --fixtures argument.

evidence.detail: The Some(native_material) arm calls config.as_ref().expect("checked above: --native-material pairs with --config").
Run exposes independently optional config/plan/native_material and a required fixtures argument.
The plan workflow documents run --plan with an explicit --native-material; Chinese counterpart has it at line 107.

title: Resource admission drops disk requirements and mistakes GPU runtime for capacity
claim: TaskRequirements retains only CPU/memory/GPU count. Disk, network and stage timeout declarations are absent from the resource comparison; any positive GPU count is accepted if a runtime name contains nvidia. The public prepare path accepts storage_mb=9000000000000 as status ok and omits it from requirements.

evidence.detail: Parser retains task_id, cpus, memory_bytes and gpus only.
gpu_runtime inspects registered Docker runtimes, not actual count/model/VRAM.
A positive GPU requirement is checked only against runtime presence; no capacity comparison.

title: Native selection still admits only the single profile-bound task
claim: A feasible task outside the one task bound by the benchmark profile is rejected as per-task native profiles are not materialized yet. Thus a general feasible multi-task native subset/full corpus cannot execute, although that capability is mandatory in the registered phase.

evidence.detail: Every selected id except the single profile-bound id is unconditionally rejected.
All three families resolve one task from one profile.
The test explicitly expects the otherwise feasible alpha-notes task to be rejected for native profile binding.

reproduction: Inspect the cited production path at c18efa83191a577f4f115b25a439febfc8ad68ad

title: A rejected rerun corrupts existing run-level evidence
claim: Reusing a completed root with a changed experiment identity overwrites run-control.json before existing trial intents cause rejection. Subsequent offline report rejects the previously valid sealed root as run-control-drift.

evidence.detail: run-control.json is overwritten unconditionally before dispatch.
Only later does native dispatch reject the existing durable intent.
Report compares the overwritten control with sealed experiment identity and refuses publication.

title: Mandatory real native and final acceptance evidence is not assessable in this audit
claim: No supplied redacted six-trial acceptance root, exact-client material or native witness archive was available to this reviewer. The executed default suite explicitly ignores seven native client/grader/Docker checks. Those fixture results cannot close real client protocol, native lifecycle, real regrade, pi-only native packaging, six-trial or final workspace exit obligations.

evidence.detail: The test module explicitly describes deterministic stand-ins and distinguishes ignored real native witnesses.
Offline regrade witnesses use stage("ok"), not pinned upstream graders.
Real acceptance requires separately supplied frozen operator evidence and cannot be waived by source inference.

reproduction: Inspect the cited production path at c18efa83191a577f4f115b25a439febfc8ad68ad

title: Published metrics do not distinguish benchmark task success from test fraction
claim: Every benchmark receives the same metric id native-grader-reward and the same generic definition. Native scalar values and valid-trial denominator survive, but no benchmark-specific definition or distinction between task success and test-case pass fraction reaches the report.

evidence.detail: The sole metrics row uses constant metric/definition strings for all benchmark revisions.
The assertion checks one benchmark label, denominator and the word zero; it never checks metric meaning or a partial pass fraction.

reproduction: Inspect the cited production path at c18efa83191a577f4f115b25a439febfc8ad68ad

title: Native trajectories fabricate measured zero Agent duration
claim: native_agent_record inserts Duration::from_secs(0) without observing Agent duration; projection serializes it as a Known wall_time_ms fact with origin supervisor-wall-clock. Missing native timing is therefore represented as measured zero rather than unknown with a reason.

evidence.detail: Native record hard-codes wall_time to zero.
That record is passed to the production ProjectionPipeline and sealed.
Projection unconditionally records Known duration with supervisor-wall-clock provenance.
